templates.label: Codex 5.3 Spark
templates.summary: Near-instant Codex worker for small focused edits, quick scans, and low-latency follow-up.
templates.description: Use for cheap parallel exploration, simple fixes, log triage, and short reviews. Escalate to Codex 5.5 when the task needs sustained reasoning, broad code changes, or sub-supervision.

templates.label: Codex 5.4 Mini
templates.summary: Fast Codex worker for lighter implementation, read-heavy scans, and parallel support tasks.
templates.description: Use when the task is bounded and speed matters more than maximum reasoning depth. Good for narrow code changes, focused audits, log summarization, and helper lanes feeding a stronger supervisor.

templates.label: Codex 5.5
templates.summary: Default Codex worker for complex coding, debugging, review, and tool-driven validation.
templates.description: Use for normal implementation lanes that need source reading, edits, tests, and follow-through. This is the default when the work is not tiny and does not require explicit high-effort reasoning.

templates.label: Codex 5.5 High
templates.summary: High-effort Codex worker for difficult root-cause analysis, broad changes, and Bus sub-supervision.
templates.description: Use when a worker should act as a sub-supervisor, use Codex App Server thread/goal tooling, investigate opaque failures, or coordinate several Codex worker lanes. Prefer this for hard blockers, security review, and cross-module changes.

templates.label: Claude Fable 5
templates.summary: Highest-capability Claude worker for long-running agents, deep research synthesis, architecture, and hard reviews.
templates.description: Use as the deep-research lead: Fable synthesizes final findings and plans, can guide Haiku extraction and Sonnet follow-through, and should use approved source URLs only. Also use for difficult architecture and multi-hour reasoning; expect slower replies.

templates.label: Claude Opus 4.8
templates.summary: Strong Claude worker for complex agentic coding, architecture review, and high-quality second opinions.
templates.description: Use for demanding implementation review, architecture alternatives, and correctness checks where quality matters more than latency. Opus is a good reviewer for a Codex lane or a fallback deep-research synthesizer.

templates.label: Claude Sonnet 5
templates.summary: Balanced Claude worker for coding, planning, and research follow-through when speed and quality both matter.
templates.description: Use for implementation follow-through after Fable or Opus research, medium-depth code review, and practical planning. Sonnet is the balanced Claude choice when the task is more than extraction but not the hardest synthesis step.

templates.label: Claude Haiku 4.5
templates.summary: Fast Claude worker for cheap parallel extraction, log triage, simple checks, and first-pass research.
templates.description: Use for parallel source extraction, finding exact quoted evidence, summarizing logs, and quick sanity checks. Haiku is best as a scout feeding a Fable, Opus, Sonnet, or Codex supervisor rather than owning hard synthesis.
